summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had a markedly elevated white blood cell count, which remained stable and asymptomatic, with no evidence of active infection. A urine test showed bacteria and white blood cells, but due to lack of symptoms, treatment was deferred. Her creatinine rose to 1.6, indicating acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, but improved to 1.3 with IV fluids. Lisinopril was held during admission. Her insulin was increased from 45 to 50 units nightly due to persistent hyperglycemia. Pain and nausea resolved with supportive care, and she tolerated oral intake. She was discharged home with follow-up plans for hematology, nephrology, and GI, along with an emergency treatment protocol for future episodes.
